A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same single-location regression study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated proofs and experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original BERT linear-probing accuracies and deterministic and stochastic PGD simulations, including temperature sensitivity experiments (Figures 1, 4, 5, and 7; Appendix D).

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds experiments with full Transformer layers and multiple-location regression (Appendix E.3, Figures 8–10).

M1.justification: The single-head erf predictor and PGD updates remain unchanged. Appendix E.3 adds a limited architectural extension: the multi-head predictor in Equation (31) sums separately parameterized erf-attention heads to predict contributions from multiple relevant tokens.

E1.justification: v2 adds actual training and evaluation on multiple-location regression, where two distinct latent tokens jointly determine the response (Equation (30), Figures 9–10). This materially extends the task beyond identifying one informative token. The original single-location simulations and synthetic sentiment datasets remain.

E2.justification: Appendix E.3 adds trained full Transformer layers, with single and multiple heads, as architectural comparisons with the simplified predictors. The optimal-linear comparison remains unchanged. Appendix F discusses MLP alternatives but does not evaluate them.

E3.justification: Original settings in Table 2 are retained. New experiments introduce fresh-sample SGD for full Transformer layers, including an 8,000-step single-head run with batch size 128 and learning rate 0.01. The multi-head simplified predictor uses 100,000 steps and freezes inverse temperature after 25,000 steps. Transformer weight extraction and post-training head matching add evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: New analyses test whether full Transformer layers reproduce the simplified model's mechanism, examining latent-direction alignment and nearly rank-one attention matrices. Figures 9–10 also investigate head specialization and reveal incomplete separation of multiple signals. The existing temperature sensitivity and NLP distribution-shift analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix E.3 specifies 20 repetitions for the single-head Transformer and simplified multi-head experiments, and 10 for the multi-head Transformer. These are run counts for new experiments, not reductions in the original experiments' 30 repetitions. The existing 95% percentile-interval reporting practice is retained.

E6.justification: Figures 8–10 add substantial findings: full Transformer layers fit the tasks, single-head weights recover the latent directions, and multi-head models achieve low risk despite incomplete parameter recovery. Appendix E.3 additionally reports a single-head attention-matrix singular-value ratio around 10^6. Original results, including Figure 1's 100% training, 95% test, and 64%/75%/69% OOD accuracies, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The principal theorems and proof arguments are retained. Appendix B.4 corrects a missing partial derivative in Lemma 14's symmetry calculation, and B.1 replaces the explicitly uniform latent-location setup with a general distribution. Appendix E.3 formally defines multiple-location regression without establishing corresponding new convergence guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions—single-location regression, asymptotic Bayes optimality, and PGD recovery—are unchanged. The conclusion modestly extends its empirical-support statement to multiple-location regression, which v1 presented only as a prospective extension.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation and applicability boundaries. It uses Transformer weight alignment to support the simplified model, interprets partial multi-head recovery as insufficient signal separation, and explicitly explains why the proof provides no quantitative convergence rate. It also discusses the analytical dependence on erf and the importance of normalization when replacing softmax.

D1.justification: Appendix E.3 adds extensive implementation information: register-token and weight initialization, model dimensions, optimization settings, multiple-location data generation, and alignment calculations. Existing code access and software disclosures remain. One new detail is ambiguous: the multi-head Transformer prose inherits an 8,000-step setup, while Figure 10 shows training through 10,000 steps.

R1.justification: New Appendix F develops substantive comparisons with Jelassi et al., Nichani et al., and Wang et al., distinguishing positional structure, token selection, and learned output projections. It also discusses MLP alternatives. Section 3 revises the softmax-replacement discussion, adding Qin et al. and Ramapuram et al. and removing Hron et al.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: the former main-text proof-outline section becomes Appendix A, the original appendices shift to B–E, and the main text proceeds from optimization to the conclusion. Related-model discussion gains a dedicated appendix. Several motivation paragraphs, captions, and mathematical explanations are tightened or expanded.

P2.justification: The paper is comprehensively reformatted into the ICLR template, changing typography, headers, spacing, and caption layouts. Figure 3 gains a side caption, Figure 6 moves with the proof outline into the appendix, and Figures 8–10 add new multi-panel experimental displays. Existing tables are restyled without changing their entries.

improvement.justification: The full Transformer experiments better support the practical relevance of the simplified analysis, while partial multi-head recovery and the convergence-rate discussion clarify its limits. Proof corrections and fuller research positioning also help. These are useful supplementary gains rather than broader theoretical guarantees; the new Figure 10 training-budget inconsistency modestly limits reproducibility.
